items.title: I've factored the RSA keys of a Certificate Authority from the 90s
items.author: ahlCVA
items.summary: Factoring RSA keys from the 90s is feasible due to advancements in computational power and algorithms. RSA-512 keys are particularly vulnerable. Modern hardware can factor these keys efficiently.

items.title: Show HN: Stuxnet – A reconstructed source code of the infamous cyber-weapon
items.author: CMDDestory
items.text: Stuxnet! Here reproduced by me. Only researchs educations purposes.
items.summary: Stuxnet is a reconstructed source code for a cyber-weapon targeting Siemens PLCs, released for educational purposes. It is not intended for real-world deployment. The original source code remains undisclosed.

items.title: Trusting-Trust Attack against an Entire Linux Distribution
items.author: signa11
items.summary: The trusting-trust attack extends beyond compilers to compromise entire Linux distributions by manipulating the GNU strip utility, affecting all binaries and ensuring persistent compromise. The attack leverages the utility's role in processing finished binaries.

items.title: Scientists observe Einstein's gravity in the quantum world
items.author: mudil
items.summary: Scientists confirmed Einstein's gravity in quantum objects, showing consistency with his theory. This was first observed in a direct experiment. The study was published in Science Advances.

items.title: John Margolies' Photographs of Roadside America
items.author: duck
items.summary: John Margolies was an American photographer known for capturing vernacular roadside architecture in the U.S. from the 1970s to 2008. His work is preserved in the John Margolies Roadside America Photograph Archive at the Library of Congress. Margolies' photographs document unique roadside attractions and commercial structures.

items.title: Show HN: I built an aesthetically pleasing puzzle
items.author: windowshopping
items.summary: An aesthetically pleasing puzzle was showcased on Hacker News. The project aims to provide an engaging and visually appealing experience. This puzzle is available at jigsawhaiku.com.

items.title: Finding a bug in Dummit and Foote's Abstract Algebra
items.author: evakhoury
items.summary: A bug was found in Dummit and Foote's Abstract Algebra regarding the first proof exercise. The function described is injective but lacks a left inverse. The book's claim was incorrect.

items.title: Colorlight 5A-75B: A dive into a popular low-cost ECP5 (FPGA) development board
items.author: gregsadetsky
items.summary: The Colorlight 5A-75B is a low-cost FPGA development board based on Lattice ECP5, supported by open-source tools, and priced around $20-$25. It's ideal for beginners and features on-board peripherals, Ethernet, and SDRAM.

items.title: Caltech Mathathon – first hackathon ever devoted to research level mathematics
items.author: astroanax
items.summary: The Caltech Mathathon is the first research-level mathematics hackathon, held October 9-11, 2026, at Caltech. Teams will solve open problems using AI. Prizes will be awarded for promising results.

items.title: Icy Moons Are Ocean Worlds
items.author: worldvoyageur
items.summary: Icy moons like Europa, Enceladus, and Titan have vast underground oceans of liquid water, potentially harboring life. Discoveries were made by missions like Voyager, Galileo, and Cassini. These moons could hold more ocean volume than Earth's oceans combined.

items.title: Decoding the NEC V20 Microcode
items.author: mariuz
items.summary: The NEC V20 is a microprocessor compatible with the Intel 8088. Its microcode was legally disputed, but found to be sufficiently different from Intel's. MartyPC decoded its microcode using die photography and machine learning.

items.title: Macbeth and His Problems
items.author: apophatic
items.summary: Macbeth's problems stem from his moral decline and lack of motivation, with his ambition driven more by Lady Macbeth than himself. The play's supernatural elements and moral complexity make it challenging to stage. Macbeth's tragic flaw is his unchecked ambition leading to tyranny.

items.title: Europe's largest carbon capture facility opens in the Netherlands
items.author: negura
items.summary: Europe's largest carbon capture facility opened in the Netherlands in 2023, capturing up to 800,000 tons of CO2 annually, and transporting it to Norway for permanent storage. This project aims to decarbonize large-scale industrial processes.

items.title: Speculative Decoding in vLLM on AMD GPUs
items.author: ankitg12
items.summary: Speculative decoding in vLLM on AMD GPUs can achieve up to 2.3x speedup. It uses draft models to predict tokens ahead of time. This improves inference throughput significantly.

items.title: Initial effects of AI technology on employment look positive
items.author: MrBuddyCasino
items.summary: Initial effects of AI technology on employment are positive, with job creation exceeding job destruction. AI is creating new roles while reshaping skill requirements. Overall, AI has led to increased employment and innovation.

items.title: Impedance Matching (2017)
items.author: muti
items.summary: Impedance matching is the practice of adjusting electrical device impedances to maximize power transfer or minimize signal reflection. It is crucial in RF systems to prevent signal reflections and ensure maximum power transfer. The goal is often to match the antenna impedance to 50 Ω for optimal performance.

items.title: Smartphone makers don't bother to comply with EU repairability requirements
items.author: mdp2021
items.summary: Despite EU repairability requirements starting in June 2025, over 80% of smartphones still lack necessary repair information. Manufacturers have not complied with rules for repair manuals and spare parts prices. Enforcement and compliance reporting need improvement.

items.title: Bill Gates tries to install MovieMaker (2003)
items.author: highfrequency
items.summary: In 2003, Bill Gates struggled to install Windows Movie Maker, criticizing its poor performance and usability. His feedback highlighted significant issues that needed addressing. This incident underscored the importance of user experience in software development.

items.title: De-Brainrot Vacations
items.author: DanielVZ
items.summary: De-brainrot vacations involve taking time off to engage in activities that reduce mental fog, like reading, nature, and socializing. Some people use this time to relearn subjects like math and physics. This trend emphasizes mental rejuvenation through breaks and new habits.

items.title: Rebuilding a 1995 GPS Time Server so I don't get Telstra'd
items.author: Brajeshwar
items.summary: Rebuilding a 1995 GPS time server involves using a Raspberry Pi and GNSS HAT for modern NTP timekeeping. The project stabilizes the onboard oscillator and revives LCD/LED indicators. Chrony and PPS support are configured for precise time synchronization.

items.title: Coop – Isolated VM Environments for Running Claude Code and Codex
items.author: aggrrrh
items.summary: Coop is an open-source tool for running AI coding agents in isolated virtual machines. It prevents risks to the host system and supports both local and cloud VMs. It is developed by Trail of Bits.
